data.name: Rogues Like Us
data.detailed_description:
Rogues Like Us is a hack n' slash rogue-lite unlike any other! Stand against a resurging threat by yourself or with a friend in local co-op. Collect weapons, armor, enchantments, and more by exploring dangerous locales and defeating powerful bosses! Stop the constructs, save the town.

The land of Arventous is perilous and combat is fast-paced, challenging you to quickly adapt to whatever stands in your way. Discover weapons, enchantments, trinkets, shrines and more to aid you on your journey. However, be warned, death carries a heavy price, requiring you to start again from the beginning, but this time with knowledge of past mistakes and new gear!

  • A UNIQUE ADVENTURE EVERY PLAY

    Fight your way through an endless number of unique dungeons! Dungeons are created through a combination of hand-crafted design and procedural generation, providing a unique experience on each play-through.

  • LOCAL CO-OP

    Adventure alone or with a friend in shared screen local co-op!

  • FIND YOUR COMBAT STYLE

    All combat stats, such as speed, damage, slam damage, etc. are weapon specific. Giving each weapon you find a unique feel and style of play.

  • EXPAND YOUR ARSENAL

    Unlock over 150 different pieces of gear, including weapons, armor, enchantments, and dyes for your future adventures!

  • A WEATHERED WORLD

    Get to know your new "friends" in the town of Recluse, or your new enemies, the constructs. Detailed descriptions of each boss and enemy you defeat are added to a bestiary in town. Every weapon or set of armor you collect gives insight into the state of the world and pages of a mysterious journal reveal long lost information.

  • ROGUISH GOOD LOOKS

    Fully customize your character by mixing and matching armor and dyes to achieve that perfect look!

reviews.review:
Rogues Like Us is an entertaining action roguelite that embraces the excitement of dungeon crawling, challenging combat, and continuous character progression while introducing enough customization to keep its adventures engaging. Developed and published by oddByte, the game transports players into the troubled land of Arventous, where dangerous constructs threaten the population and mysterious forces await discovery. Its gameplay revolves around exploring unpredictable dungeons, collecting powerful equipment, defeating increasingly formidable enemies, and learning from unsuccessful expeditions. Although its underlying formula is familiar to enthusiasts of the genre, its emphasis on weapon individuality, cooperative gameplay, and persistent equipment unlocks creates an enjoyable experience that rewards experimentation and determination.

Combat is the foundation of the experience, emphasizing quick reactions, positioning, and understanding the characteristics of different weapons. Rather than treating equipment as interchangeable tools with progressively larger damage numbers, the game gives weapons distinct attributes that influence attack speed, damage potential, and special combat properties. This encourages players to discover fighting styles that complement their preferences. Agile weapons can support aggressive engagements, while slower alternatives demand more deliberate timing. Encounters become increasingly demanding as players progress, making it important to recognize enemy behavior and avoid unnecessary risks. The combat system offers satisfying tactical possibilities, although its repetitive nature may become noticeable during extended sessions, particularly when players repeatedly encounter familiar opponents.

Dungeon exploration benefits from an interesting combination of handcrafted environments and procedural generation. Each expedition introduces different layouts and encounters, reducing the effectiveness of memorizing a single route. This unpredictability encourages players to remain attentive and adjust their strategies according to available resources. Discovering shrines, trinkets, enchantments, and valuable equipment adds excitement to exploration, especially when unexpected rewards improve an otherwise difficult run. However, procedural variation does not completely eliminate repetition. Players will eventually recognize recurring environmental elements and combat situations, meaning the experience depends heavily on their enjoyment of repeated dungeon expeditions rather than a constantly evolving campaign.

Equipment progression provides one of the strongest incentives to continue playing. With more than 150 unlockable items, including weapons, armor, enchantments, and cosmetic dyes, the game offers substantial opportunities for personalization. Experimenting with different combinations can change how players approach encounters, while cosmetic customization allows them to create characters with distinctive appearances. The progression system also makes failure somewhat easier to accept because new equipment and accumulated knowledge can contribute to future attempts. Nevertheless, death remains consequential, forcing players to begin another expedition rather than simply continuing from their previous position. This creates a rewarding cycle of improvement for dedicated players but may frustrate those who prefer consistent advancement without significant setbacks.

The worldbuilding adds welcome personality to what could otherwise have been a straightforward combat experience. The town of Recluse provides a connection to the wider setting, while the mysterious constructs establish a central threat. Much of the narrative is communicated through equipment descriptions, journal entries, and an expanding bestiary that records information about defeated enemies and bosses. This method encourages curiosity and rewards players who enjoy uncovering stories through exploration. However, the narrative takes a secondary role to gameplay, and anyone expecting elaborate conversations, extensive character development, or cinematic storytelling may find the presentation relatively restrained. Its greatest narrative strength is creating enough mystery to give repeated adventures a sense of purpose.

Another appealing feature is the inclusion of shared-screen local cooperative gameplay. Exploring dangerous environments alongside a friend introduces additional entertainment through coordinated attacks, shared discoveries, and cooperative survival. Steam Remote Play Together further expands accessibility by allowing players to experience the local multiplayer functionality remotely. The game also lists shared-screen competitive multiplayer support, although cooperative dungeon crawling remains its more distinctive attraction. These features provide welcome flexibility, especially for players who enjoy smaller multiplayer experiences. However, those expecting dedicated online matchmaking or large cooperative parties should recognize the limitations of its multiplayer structure.

Visually, the game adopts a colorful fantasy presentation that complements its energetic combat and adventurous atmosphere. Its environments, equipment designs, and character customization contribute to an approachable identity without relying on elaborate graphical effects. The overall presentation is relatively modest, but that simplicity suits the game's independent development scope. Its lightweight system requirements are another advantage for players using less powerful computers. Still, visual variety alone cannot entirely disguise the repeated nature of dungeon exploration, and some players may eventually desire greater environmental diversity or more elaborate enemy encounters.

Steam Deck compatibility remains officially Unknown or Unverified, as no confirmed Steam Deck Verified or Playable designation is displayed on the Steam store listing. Although its relatively modest hardware requirements suggest that performance demands should be manageable, successful operation through SteamOS and Proton cannot be guaranteed. Controller functionality, interface readability, and potential compatibility adjustments should be considered before purchasing specifically for handheld use. Players interested in the portable experience may need to experiment with compatibility settings or community controller configurations.

Ultimately, Rogues Like Us succeeds through its enjoyable combat mechanics, substantial equipment collection, unpredictable dungeon layouts, and cooperative possibilities. Its greatest accomplishment is making different weapons feel meaningful while encouraging players to develop their skills through repeated adventures. The experience is not without weaknesses, particularly its potentially repetitive structure, punishing restarts, and comparatively limited storytelling. Nevertheless, these shortcomings are unlikely to overshadow its appeal for players who appreciate challenging action roguelites built around experimentation and gradual mastery. It offers a worthwhile adventure for those willing to embrace failure as part of progression and enjoy discovering new approaches to familiar challenges.

A rewarding indie dungeon crawler with satisfying weapon variety, extensive customization, and enjoyable cooperative gameplay, held back slightly by repetitive encounters and unforgiving progression.

Rating: 8/10
